blinding_note: Model, workflow name, tokens, runtimes and tool traces are withheld. Reviewers must disclose if report content still reveals the method.
objective: Investigate cultivation variability with supporting and contradictory evidence and competing hypotheses; do not assert proven causes.

report.assessment: The supplied evidence supports several cultivation-variability signals and data-quality alerts, but does not establish causes, specification failures, or exact event onset. The investigation is partial: evidence consists mainly of selected source observations and screening summaries, not a complete review of the underlying series or operating records.

candidate_reviews.reason: Source observations support a reflection peak followed by a lower final sampled value. An expected end-of-run change, measurement behavior, and process change remain competing explanations; no operating threshold is supplied.

The screening summary flags backwards source-time patterns across permittivity channels, but supplied observations do not expose the sequence needed to verify chronology. Possible reset, out-of-order acquisition, or clock/data handling remain open.

The cited peaks differ markedly, but are from separate reactors and may be at different times. Reactor design, sensor status, and measurement comparability are unresolved; this is not evidence of failure by itself.

The cited cumulative-feed endpoints are both zero. This could reflect an intentional no-feed condition, an unpopulated or mis-mapped series, or a logging issue; inspect the feed plan and raw channel before interpreting it.

The CO2 aeration observations show a nonzero sampled value and a zero final value. Planned shutdown or endpoint logging are plausible alternatives to an interruption; termination alone does not establish physical interruption.
The two reactor fitting-error peaks are very different, but their timings differ and peak magnitude alone does not establish fit validity, process severity, or design-equivalent comparison.
The cited cumulative-feed endpoints are both zero. No feed may be intentional; a channel, mapping, or logging issue is also possible. Feed records and full traces are needed.

The screening summary flags backwards source-time patterns in permittivity data. A reset, acquisition ordering, or clock/data handling are competing hypotheses; chronology cannot be resolved from the selected values alone.

The cited aeration observations show a nonzero sampled value and a zero final value. Planned shutdown or recording conventions remain alternatives to an interruption; no physical cause is established.

The two reactors have different cited cumulative-NaOH peaks at different sampled times. Different process demand, duration, recipe, or measurement behavior could account for the contrast; design equivalence is not established.
The cited agitation observations are constant across the sampled span, which may be the intended operating setpoint. This does not establish a control or logging fault.

Offline lactate observations show a lower later sampled value than an earlier observed maximum. Biological consumption, sampling/assay variation, and expected process progression are competing explanations; these samples do not establish exact onset or cause.

cross_scope_synthesis: Paired reactor observations show both broadly similar and notably different sampled dissolved-CO2 values; this does not by itself show that reactors were intended to be equivalent. See C003 and C004.
The evidence includes process, offline, and sensor-data signals, but source summaries and selected timepoints cannot establish a common cause or exact onset.
Screening alerts for endpoint changes, constant series, and backwards source time require contextual and source-level review rather than being treated as failures.

Extend the investigation to all underlying time series and replicate-level summaries before making a batch-level variability or performance conclusion.
